qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Statutory regional monopoly licence providing water and wastewater services across North West England. Formulaic RCV indexation to CPIH inflation provides inflation pass-through with captive regional customer base. Key risks include Ofwat regulatory tightening, environmental fines over storm overflows, and political scrutiny.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet). United Utilities possesses an entrenched statutory water and wastewater monopoly in North West England with CPIH-linked revenue indexing. However, regulatory allowed ROIC is capped at ~5.5%, and the business faces perpetual capital dilution with AMP8 requiring ~£13B in totex. Balance sheet leverage is excessive with £11.2B in debt (19x net income) and interest coverage of 2.98x, failing the >5x infrastructure threshold and violating Gate 6 peace-of-mind solvency requirements.
qualitative.evidence: Statutory water and wastewater provider serving 7.4 million people in North West England. FY2025 revenue of £2,616.3M and operating profit of £1,172.9M. 4-year median GAAP ROIC is 5.55% (4.04%-7.94%), anchored by Ofwat regulated cost of capital. Total long-term debt of £11,235.4M and net debt of £9,441.1M against TTM net income of £586.8M yields a Debt / Net Income ratio of 19.1x. EBIT / Interest coverage of 2.98x (£1,172.9M / £393.9M) falls well below the 5.0x minimum threshold for infrastructure assets. Capex of £1,535.0M exceeds D&A (£500.5M) by 3x, with ~£13B AMP8 commitments ensuring persistent negative post-capex free cash flow and perpetual reliance on debt capital markets.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
